# Issue #41: `slugify` produces double hyphens and trailing hyphens

`slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello--world-"` but should return `"hello-world"`.
Also `slugify("--a--b--")` should give `"a-b"`.

Please fix `textkit/slug.py`. Do not change the public signature.

content: Fixed. The issue was in `textkit/slug.py`: the regex `[^a-z0-9]` replaced each non-alphanumeric character individually with a hyphen, so consecutive punctuation/whitespace produced multiple hyphens, and leading/trailing characters produced edge hyphens. I changed the pattern to `[^a-z0-9]+` (collapse runs into a single hyphen) and added `.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens. The public signature is unchanged, tests pass, and both reported cases now return the expected output (`"hello-world"` and `"a-b"`).

arguments.summary: Fixed slugify in textkit/slug.py by changing the replacement regex from [^a-z0-9] to [^a-z0-9]+ so runs of non-alphanumeric characters collapse into a single hyphen, and added .strip("-") to remove leading/trailing hyphens. Public signature unchanged; existing tests pass and both issue cases (slugify("Hello,  World!") -> "hello-world", slugify("--a--b--") -> "a-b") now behave correctly.
